prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell), ATFM/A-CDM layer; airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; recalculates capacity from confirmed airport position, never originates airfield safety judgments); Slot Allocation Engine; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display, records duty desk confirmations); Digital Briefing Room; Tower Sequence Manager (never replaces controllers); Ramp Movement Board (primary view: planned apron movements, conflicts, towing, stand occupancy); Departure Metering Service; Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console (degraded channel for tower/duty desk decisions when Portal down); Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard); Flight Data Exchange; Surface Surveillance Adapter (East/West Apron Sensors; sends position, stand occupancy, lane blocking to Portal and Ramp Control Lead); Airline Interface Adapter; Alert Distribution Hub (sends approved duty alerts on runway/taxi/apron changes); Performance Analytics Warehouse (planned vs actual; duty events vs movements); Audit Event Ledger; Identity Access Service (only authorized airport staff enter confirmations, logs to Ledger); Business Rules Registry (BRR); Time Synchronization Service; Collaborative Decision Log; North/South Runway Meter; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector. Platform receives confirmed capacity impacts after local duty coordination. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron): FIM, TOBT; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Ramp Control Lead (Quartzline): sequences pushbacks, stand exits/entries, towing; Tower Supervisor (Brindle): verifies runway-use reductions; Slot Coordinator: CTT feasibility; Airport Duty Manager: duty desk, Airport Capacity Plan, confirms modes, verifies airfield checks before AAR/metering changes, briefs handover; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer; others (Network Ops Liaison, Deicing Coordinator, Emergency Response Coordinator, etc.). Items: FIM, Airport Capacity Plan, TOBT, CTT, Airport Acceptance Rate, Tactical Regulation Proposal, Ground Delay Program status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Post Operations Report, weather condition update, duty coordination alert. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase. Requirements: Orchard shall issue time-stamped weather updates; Ramp Control Lead shall not release pushback until Tower Supervisor confirms integration with

New part:
S205: East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor indications are used as supporting evidence, but the Ramp Control Lead remains responsible for reconciling sensor data with visual and operational reports.
S206: The Ramp Control Lead assigns priority to towing movements that remove a blocking aircraft, protect a confirmed departure sequence, or create capacity for an inbound aircraft with no equivalent stand option.
S207: Routine maintenance tows are normally sequenced behind live departure and arrival movements unless an operational safety issue requires earlier action.
S208: Ramp Control Lead sends the Stand Tow Request Form when a parked aircraft must be repositioned to release a stand, remove an apron blockage, or support a confirmed operating plan.
S209: Apron occupancy is managed as a time-based resource, with each stand treated as unavailable from the start of servicing until the aircraft and equipment are clear of the marked safety area.
S210: The Gate Conflict Detector alerts the Ramp Control Lead when a planned arrival, departure, or tow would create an overlapping occupancy condition at a stand or adjacent service lane.
S211: When a conflict is detected, the Ramp Control Lead coordinates with the Ground Handling Dispatcher to confirm whether servicing progress, equipment availability, or staffing constraints can change the sequence.
S212: The Handling Resource Planner provides the shared planning basis for baggage, catering, cleaning, boarding support, and towing resources that affect apron readiness.
S213: The Ramp Control Lead reviews Handling Resource Planner constraints before committing to a pushback sequence that depends on rapid equipment removal or immediate stand reuse.
S214: Airline Operations Coordinator participation is required when a resequence would materially affect passenger boarding, connection protection, or aircraft rotation plans.
S215: The Aircraft Operator Representative remains accountable for operator acceptance of any revised off-block expectation that results from ramp resequencing.
S216: Marlinstone shall refresh stand demand forecasts when the Ramp Movement Board records a material change in planned off-block timing.
S217: The Tower Sequence Manager receives the current ramp intent through system synchronization so that apron releases and runway metering remain consistent.
S218: If apron congestion begins to affect runway delivery, the Ramp Control Lead escalates the condition to the Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager for a coordinated mitigation decision.
S219: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Ramp Control Lead increases spacing between pushbacks and towing movements to account for slower ground servicing and reduced driver visibility.
S220: During Capacity Reduction State, apron movements are prioritized to prevent stand saturation and to preserve access for emergency routes and critical service lanes.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
